name: Porcelain insulator
region: Britain, Germany and the United States
summary: Glazed porcelain that holds a live wire away from a pole or a tower. The shape follows the electric field and the rain: a stack of skirts, a brown or grey glaze, and a cement joint to a metal cap.

philosophy.core_thesis: A wire needs a dry, hard, glazed surface between it and the earth, so the clay body is dense and the shape is a stack of rain skirts.
design_principles: Fire a dense body with water absorption below 0.5 %, so that no moisture enters the wall.
Glaze every outer surface 0.3 to 0.5 mm thick, in brown or light grey, to shed rain and dirt.
Shape the outer face as 2 to 4 skirts that overhang, so that the inner face stays dry in rain.
Grow the creepage path with the voltage: about 20 to 25 mm of surface for each kV of line voltage.
Leave a ring of the glaze off the cement seat and coat it with sand, so that the cement holds.
Make a suspension disc 146 mm across and 254 mm apart in a string, so that parts fit each other.
Stamp the maker, the year and the load on the shoulder in raised or incised letters.
anti_patterns: A thin white pot with a gold line and a floral print
A porous body that shows a bare, rough surface under the glaze
A single smooth cylinder with no skirt to break the water film
Bright colour glaze that hides tracking marks and dirt
A hand-painted pattern on the skirt

form.shape: Bell-shaped pin insulators for a cross-arm, stacked disc units for a string, solid post insulators, and bushings with a stack of skirts.
form.profile: A smooth dome at the top, then 2 to 4 skirts that flare out and curl under, with a deep groove at the neck for the wire.
form.foot_and_rim: A threaded socket or a sanded cement seat at the foot, and a rolled, thick rim on each skirt so that it does not chip.
form.proportion: Pin insulator 100 to 300 mm tall, wall 10 to 25 mm thick; each skirt reaches out 25 to 40 mm past the one above.
rules: Keep the skirt rim thick and round: a thin edge chips in transport.
Keep the wall the same thickness all round, so that it fires without cracks.
Put the wire groove at the top or neck, on a clean glaze.
Leave a sanded, unglazed band where the metal cap is cemented.

bodies.rule: Use a dense, grey-white technical porcelain of clay, feldspar and quartz or alumina. A fired break must be glassy and show no pores.

methods: wet-process throwing and turning on a lathe
leather-hard turning and joining of units
cement assembly of cap and pin
forming.joins: A cast iron cap and a steel pin are cemented to the sanded porcelain; large units join from 2 or 3 fired pieces with cement.
forming.details: A stamped mark of the maker on the shoulder, a thin ring where the glaze stops, and three small spur marks on the foot.

glaze.pattern: No pattern. The only marks are the skirts, the raised ribs, the maker's stamp and the load rating in raised letters.
glaze.gloss: High gloss, about 80 to 95 GU, on a smooth, hard glaze with no pinholes.
glaze.wear: Dust and soot dull the glaze in time; the surface stays hard, and a chip shows the white body under a brown glaze.

palette.strategy: A restrained brown, grey or white glaze with a sanded band of grey, and a dark metal cap.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired round downdraught kiln, later a gas or electric tunnel kiln, with saggars for the large units.
processes: dry the unit slowly for days
fire in one pass at 1250 to 1400 °C
assemble the cap and pin with cement
firing.scale: A factory with tunnel kilns; a long string for a 400 kV line holds some 20 to 30 discs.
firing.signs: A thin glaze ring at the foot, kiln stilt marks, a maker stamp and a test mark; a small pinhole or a sag shows a reject.

pieces.form: Pin insulator with 2 skirts and a wire groove at the top
Disc unit for a suspension string with a deep rain skirt
Post insulator, a column with 6 ribs and a grey glaze
Glazed crucible with a lid for a laboratory furnace

positive: stacked rain skirts on a pole
cement joint to a galvanised cap
stamped maker mark on the shoulder
power line hardware against a grey sky

evidence.title: Porcelain insulator on an electric fence

emotion.target_response: A plain, hard order: the viewer sees a part that has one job, and thinks of lines on a hill and a dry sky after rain.

use_cases: an industrial still-life with power line hardware
a technical brief for a glazed electrical part
a collector label for a telegraph insulator
avoid_when: the brief needs a glass or polymer insulator

modifiers.how: Change to a thin white hard-paste body, remove the skirts and add overglaze painting and gilt.
Change to vitreous china with a thick white glaze and cast it in a plaster mould.

wall_thickness.note: Large units for high voltage have thick walls; small pin insulators are thinner.
